subfamily: the first Daiquiri's form as Oxford reports the family account (DAIQUIRI pdf 621: rum, limes from his garden, sugar, swizzled in a pitcher with shaved ice), made for six; core white rum, balance lime and sugar dissolved in the lime (no syrup), seasoning makrut lime leaves pressed in and taken out (Codex p. 117: 'Fragrant leaves are great for muddling and infusions')
glass: six small tumblers (about 180 ml), chilled, poured from one pitcher (about 1.5 litres) with the crushed ice
version: v1 (Tomás, round 2, 2026-10-04). Judged on Arnold's shaken (sours) ranges: a pitcher swizzled on crushed ice for 30 seconds dilutes like a shake (as Off the Tour's swizzle), with melt swept by hand (freeform + water): 40% melt OUT-ish sharp (19.9%, 0.993% acid), 45% sharp (0.959), 56.6% as modelled, 65-75% all in range, 85% on the floors (15.0%, 0.752 acid). So the method fixes the ice (about 500 g), the time (30 s) and pours at once. Rejected on paper: 300/150 ml lime/75 g sugar (OUT on sugar and acid), 300/120/60 (OUT on acid), 300/112.5/55 (OUT on initial acid). Strength swept 37.5-50%: 37.5-45% all in; 50% OUT on strength (21.5%), so the rum is 37.5-45%. Sugar dissolved dry in the lime keeps the story's three things (rum, lime, sugar) and adds 0.63 ml per g, not a syrup's water.
